title: quantization-performance-quality-benchmarks-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-kernels
body:
Summary:

This working doc captures our recent end-to-end benchmarks and profiler traces comparing INT8 (GPTQ & AWQ), FP8, and FP16 baselines across different low-level kernel implementations. Focus is on throughput (tokens/sec), tail latency (p95/p99), and quality regression (perplexity & MMLU-style accuracy). Primary goal: provide guidance for which quantization stack to use in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments and identify kernel-level bottlenecks we should optimize in the runtime.

Key takeaways (short):
- INT8 (GPTQ) gives the best throughput uplift vs FP16 with modest quality drop; AWQ-int8 closes much of the quality gap at ~similar perf.
- FP8 yields highest throughput in microbenchmarks but is more sensitive to kernel stability and operator support (especially on A100 kernels).
- GEMM (matmul) kernels dominate runtime (>60% of total time). Attention and KV-cache handling are non-trivial secondary hotspots.
- Fused int8 matmul kernels + per-channel scales reduce overhead and improve p99 latency more than naive quantize-dequantize strategies.

Benchmarks (representative):
Hardware: single NVIDIA A100-80GB (PCIe env for reproducibility)
Model: LLaMA-2-7B-v1 (fp16 baseline weights) served with autoregressive sampling, temperature=0.7
Prompt mix: 50% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (256 tokens), 20% long (1024 tokens) — synthetic mix reflecting chat workloads
Batching: dynamic batching enabled, max batch 8, target latency SLO = 200ms
Metrics captured: throughput (tokens/sec), p95/p99 latency (ms), memory footprint (GB), eval quality (perplexity on WikiText-ish heldout, small MMLU probe subset)

Results (aggregated):
- FP16 baseline:
  - throughput: 480 tok/s
  - p95 latency: 18.2 ms
  - memory (model + KV): 46.8 GB
  - perplexity: 12.4
  - MMLU probe accuracy: 67.4%

- INT8 (GPTQ, per-channel, block size 128):
  - throughput: 820 tok/s (+70% vs FP16)
  - p95 latency: 10.1 ms
  - memory: 28.6 GB (-39%)
  - perplexity: 12.8 (+3.2%)
  - MMLU probe accuracy: 66.2% (-1.2 pp)

- INT8 (AWQ, per-channel, block size 128, mixed-FP8 scales for activations):
  - throughput: 760 tok/s (+58% vs FP16)
  - p95 latency: 10.9 ms
  - memory: 29.1 GB (-38%)
  - perplexity: 12.6 (+1.6%)
  - MMLU probe accuracy: 66.8% (-0.6 pp)

- FP8 (E4M3 style emulated with custom kernels):
  - throughput: 920 tok/s (+92% vs FP16)
  - p95 latency: 9.0 ms
  - memory: 24.5 GB (-48%)
  - perplexity: 12.5 (+0.8%)
  - MMLU probe accuracy: 67.1% (-0.3 pp)

Notes on numbers: these are single-machine, single-GPU measurements and include runtime overhead (tokenization + decoding). Throughput numbers are tokens/sec observed at the RPC boundary. Quality probes use a fixed eval set; we report relative changes (absolute differences small but meaningful for regression alarms).

Profiler breakdown (sample run, INT8 GPTQ):
- GEMM kernels (matmul): ~62% of total time
- Attention + softmax: ~8%
- KV cache read/write & memcopies: ~7%
- Layernorm + activation quant/dequant overhead: ~6%
- Decoder tokenization/IO + scheduling: ~5%
- Other (per-layer bookkeeping, thread sync): ~12%

Hotspots & Observations:
1) GEMM remains the dominant hotspot. Even with quantized weights, quant-aware matmul kernels are critical; naive quantize-dequant around FP16 GEMMs loses most of the benefit.
2) Memory bandwidth and L2 cache thrashing are the limiting factors for larger batch sizes — FP8 reduces memory pressure best, which explains the higher throughput in microbenchmarks.
3) AWQ vs GPTQ: AWQ shows better robustness on rare tokens / long contexts (smaller perplexity delta), but costs ~5-8% throughput vs GPTQ in our kernel implementations.
4) FP8 provides the best throughput but requires careful kernel selection and fallback strategies since some older drivers / cuBLAS versions show numeric instability for particular GEMM shapes.
5) KV-cache handling for long-context prompts surfaced a non-trivial cost: quantized KV read/write path (packing/unpacking) added measurable decode latency on our first pass.
6) Per-channel scales + block quantization (block size 32–128 tried) is a sweet spot; very small blocks improve quality slightly but increase quant/dequant overhead.

Microbench kernel tests (single-op isolated):
- Int8-fused-gemm (custom kernel): achieves 2.1x speed vs FP16 cuBLAS GEMM for 4096x4096 matmul at B=1
- FP8 emu kernel (fused reduce + cast): ~2.6x speed vs FP16 for same shape, but variance across matmul shapes higher
- cuBLAS int8 INT8x32 kernel fallback showed lower stability for some odd-even shapes — needs test coverage in CI

Quality checks (failure modes observed):
- Rare token generation: GPTQ-int8 shows slightly more hallucinations in a small set of factual QA prompts vs FP16; AWQ mitigates most of this.
- Long-context coherence: FP8 maintained coherence almost indistinguishable from FP16 on 1k-token stories; GPTQ-int8 saw small drift in factual consistency over 800+ tokens in a few runs.

Operational considerations for serving:
- Canary strategy: rollout AWQ-int8 behind a canary for high-quality routes (chat assistant) with automatic rollback if eval set perplexity increases >2.0% or MMLU drops >1.0pp.
- Cost tiering: use GPTQ-int8 for low-cost background tasks (batch reranking, embeddings) where small quality loss acceptable.
- Fallbacks: if custom int8/FP8 kernel fails or triggers NaN, fallback to FP16 to maintain availability. Log full trace to S3 for postmortem.
- CV/QA integration: add signal to console to correlate user-reported quality regressions with quantization changes (prompt set matching).

Recommendations (short-term roadmap):
- Add focused kernel optimizations for int8 fused-gemm (reduce load/store, tune for A100 L2) — PR target: serving-runtime#445
- Implement packed-quantized KV-cache path to avoid per-token unpacking overhead; test memory-vs-latency tradeoffs.
- Expand QA eval set: long-context story coherence + factual QA + open-domain factuality probes; automate daily checkpoint comparisons to detect regressions.
- Harden FP8 path: add shape-specific fallbacks and driver-version checks; run stress tests across cuBLAS/cuDNN versions.
- Add microbench CI job that runs a representative set of matmul shapes across kernels on startup.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need systematic experiments on H100 (SXM) and cheaper SKUs (T4, A10) — will performance and stability patterns change? (assign: Miguel)
- Should we invest in quantization-aware fine-tuning for AWQ to close remaining gaps for low-temp generation? (assign: Priya)
- Quantization scale persistence: can we reuse computed scales across minor model updates to speed conversion in Dedicated/Private deployments? (investigate)
- Kernel rollout safety: define non-blocking telemetry (per-prompt perplexity probes) for hosted customers to detect silent regressions.

Appendix: experiment config details (condensed) - sampling: top_p=0.95, temperature=0.7, max_new_tokens=512 - quantization configs tried: GPTQ (per-channel, block=128/64/32), AWQ (per-channel + mixed activation FP8 scaling), FP8 (E4M3 emulated + custom kernels) - dataset for perplexity: heldout subset derived from WikiText-like crawl (~10k tokens per run) - evaluation MMLU probe: small 200-question subset representative of reasoning/general knowledge

Next steps before wider rollout:
1) Run full E2E nightly job comparing FP16 vs AWQ-int8 vs GPTQ-int8 vs FP8 across 10k prompt mix and upload traces + profiler outputs. (owner: Samira)
2) Kernel optimization sprint (2 weeks) to land fused int8-gemm improvements and packed KV path (owners: Daniel + Evan)
3) Add CI job for matmul shape stability across driver versions (owner: Miguel)

If you have additional prompts or specific customer workload shapes we should include in the next run, add them to ENGINF-842.

-- Samira
